bounds: One mapped event, unchanged/changed/deleted provider version, clean/held link and current/retired owner. The sequential read-reconcile-project path reaches projection in two steps without fairness assumptions. Existing reconciler tests cover revision races and uncertain writes; this model does not prove provider availability or the live UI. The local revision is fixed in these cases; concurrent authorized local edits and provider mutations remain covered by the existing shared reconciler tests, not by NoProviderWrites in this model. A readable managed observation enters the canonical cache even without linked-write permission. Absent events are not erased by a bounded feed. The owning real-store test verifies persistence before selected-event lookup. The cache-drain case covers one service, two calendars in either the same or different grants, one purge with at most one pre-deletion failure and retry, one optional fresh post-purge read, binary complete/invalid broker results, cancellation before or after write admission, and successful/failed persistence. The grant admission lock fences new reads while all registered per-calendar tails drain; separate calendars remain concurrent and unrelated grants are preserved. A purge is not revocation: reads admitted after its receipt may import while the source remains enabled. A write admitted before cancellation may commit, but the read cannot report success and purge drains it. One symbolic event per calendar represents its whole payload. Concrete real-store hooks require all54 named mapped/feed/diagnostic cases without skips, including the four-read bound, removal, cancelled write drain, invalid feeds and selected cache persistence. The old mapped model fixes local revisions; post-lock reconciliation uses existing Eliza-only CAS/restore ports and cannot reinsert a Google projection. Fair purge progress assumes broker completion, persistence settlement (success or failure), and purge settlement/retry after the single modeled failure; an unfair stuttering counterexample is required. Multi-process ordering, transaction rollback, arbitrary provider response sizes, broker/provider authority, and provider eventual consistency remain outside this finite service projection.

assumptions: Weak fairness of broker response, cache-write settlement (including failure), removal and retry. At most one pre-deletion removal failure; provider success and new admission are not assumed.
No fairness: a held broker read or pending persistence may stutter forever.
